fields.title: What a certificate buys
fields.keyTakeaway: Certification pays off when deals are blocked by its absence, while preparation without certification delivers most of the internal value and is needed anyway.
fields.sections/0/blocks/0/text: The client asks about SOC 2. Do we need to get it?
fields.sections/1/blocks/0/text: [[certification|Certification]] takes months of work and noticeable money, and it is often obtained out of inertia — because "everyone has it." The decision must rest on your segment and what the certificate replaces.
fields.sections/2/blocks/0/text: **[[term-5|Common standards]]** confirm that the company has information security processes in place and running. They do not guarantee the absence of vulnerabilities — they confirm the presence of processes.
fields.sections/2/blocks/2/text: *Shorter questionnaires.* Instead of answering 40 items, you attach a report. Saves weeks on every deal. *Access to a segment.* Some large clients will not consider vendors without a certificate. *Internal discipline.* Preparation forces you to get your processes in order.
fields.sections/2/blocks/4/text: *Preparation.* 3 to 9 months, depending on the starting state. *Audit.* Money, annually. *Maintenance.* Constant discipline: logs, access reviews, training, incidents.
fields.sections/2/blocks/5/text: When it pays off: **when deals hit a wall due to the lack of a certificate.** Calculated directly: how many deals and for what amount are blocked.
fields.sections/2/blocks/6/text: When it does not: a product for small businesses or consumers where no one asks.
fields.sections/2/blocks/7/text: Intermediate option: **prepare without getting certified.** Bring processes into compliance, answer questionnaires in detail, and get the certificate when the first deal requiring it appears. Delivers most of the internal value without the audit cost.
fields.sections/3/blocks/0/text: The question came up twice, the answer changed.
fields.sections/3/blocks/1/text: *First time,* at the first enterprise deal. Calculated: one deal, the questionnaire is handled by answers, the certificate costs half a year. Declined, passed the questionnaire.
fields.sections/3/blocks/2/text: *Second time,* with three retail chains in negotiations and two active. One chain listed the certificate as desirable rather than mandatory. Calculated differently: does not pay off yet, but the preparation does — getting processes in order is necessary anyway.
fields.sections/3/blocks/3/text: What they did: processing register, access reviews, team training, incident and breach procedures, logs. All of these were covered in previous blocks and would have been needed regardless.
fields.sections/3/blocks/4/text: The certification decision is postponed with a condition: we get it when the first deal is blocked by its absence. Recorded with an owner and a semi-annual review.
fields.sections/4/blocks/0/text: A certificate is not an indicator of security, but an indicator of having processes. A company with a certificate can have vulnerabilities; a company without one can be better protected.
fields.sections/5/blocks/0/text: Certification pays off when deals are blocked by its absence, while preparation without certification delivers most of the internal value and is needed anyway.
